book.title: Anger: Wisdom for Cooling the Flames
book.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

confidence_note: Only the seed passage and selective watering are confirmed (verbatim quotes). The old title's 'disconnected mind' angle and criticism example could not be confirmed.
facts: The main cause of suffering is the seed of anger in you.
The seed has been watered too often, by yourself and by other people.
Selective watering protects you and your beloved ones.
Try not to say or do anything when angry; begin mindful breathing right away.
tension: The trigger is outside, the seed is inside.
opening_idea: A seed does nothing until watered.

lessons.idea: Look for the seed under the anger.
lessons.anchor: seed watered by self and others

reflect_final: Which thought or habit of yours carried water to your last anger?

use_cases.move: I'm going to stop watering this seed and go for a walk.

use_cases.situation: Someone at home made you angry
use_cases.move: I'm angry and part of that is mine. I'll calm down and talk.

use_cases.situation: A comment in a meeting angers you
use_cases.move: That hit me. I'll breathe and think again before answering.

pocket_idea: The seed of anger is inside you; which seed you water is yours to choose.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The main cause is a seed watered too often.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Seed, water by self and others, selective watering, breathing.
